next:wr:940.hint: この博物館を訪れるのは価値がある
next:wr:940.answer: It is worth while to visit this museum.
next:wr:940.fullSentence: It is worth while to visit this museum.
next:wr:940.explanation: It is worth while to do A『Aをするのは価値がある』。
next:wr:940.relatedInfo: It is worthwhile doing A. とも言える。

next:wr:942.hint: これらの古い文書は歴史家にとって非常に価値がある
next:wr:942.answer: These old documents are priceless to historians.
next:wr:942.fullSentence: These old documents are priceless to historians.
next:wr:942.explanation: priceless = invaluable『非常に価値がある』。
next:wr:942.relatedInfo: 『値段がつけられないほど』が転じて非常に価値があるという意味に。

next:wr:944.hint: 彼女は3か国語を流暢に話すことができる(人が主語)
next:wr:944.answer: She is able to speak three languages fluently.
next:wr:944.fullSentence: She is able to speak three languages fluently.
next:wr:944.explanation: (人) be able to do『(人が)〜できる』。
next:wr:944.relatedInfo: It is possible for A to do(物事が主語)との対比。

next:wr:946.hint: この機械は大量のデータを処理する能力がある
next:wr:946.answer: This machine is capable of processing huge amounts of data.
next:wr:946.fullSentence: This machine is capable of processing huge amounts of data.
next:wr:946.explanation: A is capable of doing『Aは〜する能力がある』。
next:wr:946.relatedInfo: be able to doとほぼ同義だが、機械などの性能にもよく使う。

next:wr:948.hint: 彼は帰宅途中にコンビニに立ち寄った
next:wr:948.answer: He stopped at a convenience store on his way home.
next:wr:948.fullSentence: He stopped at a convenience store on his way home.
next:wr:948.explanation: on one's way home『帰宅途中に』。
next:wr:948.relatedInfo: on one's way to Aで『Aに行く途中に』にもなる。

next:wr:950.hint: 赤ちゃんは9時までにぐっすり眠っていた
next:wr:950.answer: The baby was sound asleep by nine o'clock.
next:wr:950.fullSentence: The baby was sound asleep by nine o'clock.
next:wr:950.explanation: sound asleep = fast asleep『ぐっすり眠っている』。
next:wr:950.relatedInfo: soundは形容詞asleepを強調する副詞的用法。

next:wr:952.hint: この作業であなたの助けがぜひとも必要だ(動詞の強調)
next:wr:952.answer: I badly need your help with this task.
next:wr:952.fullSentence: I badly need your help with this task.
next:wr:952.explanation: badly + miss/want/need『とても、ぜひ〜』(動詞の強調)。
next:wr:952.relatedInfo: badlyが『悪く』ではなく『強く』の意味になる特殊用法。

next:wr:954.hint: 彼女は私に親しみのこもった笑顔を向けた
next:wr:954.answer: She gave me a friendly smile.
next:wr:954.fullSentence: She gave me a friendly smile.
next:wr:954.explanation: friendlyは名詞friend+lyでできた形容詞(副詞ではない)。
next:wr:954.relatedInfo: -lyがついていても形容詞である例外的な単語。

next:wr:956.hint: 近ごろ、在宅勤務をする人が増えている(現在形とともに)
next:wr:956.answer: These days, more people are working from home.
next:wr:956.fullSentence: These days, more people are working from home.
next:wr:956.explanation: these days, nowadays『近ごろ』(現在形とともに使う)。
next:wr:956.relatedInfo: lately, recently(過去形・完了形とともに使う)との対比。

next:wr:958.hint: 試合前に天気が回復して幸いだった
next:wr:958.answer: It is fortunate that the weather cleared up before the game.
next:wr:958.fullSentence: It is fortunate that the weather cleared up before the game.
next:wr:958.explanation: It is fortunate that ~『幸いなことに〜』。
next:wr:958.relatedInfo: 形式主語itを使った感情・評価を表す構文。

next:wr:960.hint: このレストランはかなり高価だ
next:wr:960.relatedInfo: low/highはpriceに、cheap/expensiveは商品自体に使う。

next:wr:962.hint: 番号をお間違えのようです
next:wr:962.answer: I think you have the wrong number.
next:wr:962.fullSentence: I think you have the wrong number.
next:wr:962.explanation: the wrong A(number, direction)『間違った〜(番号・方向など)』。

next:wr:964.hint: 彼は3年前にその会社を辞めた(過去形とともに)
next:wr:964.answer: He left the company three years ago.
next:wr:964.fullSentence: He left the company three years ago.
next:wr:964.explanation: ago『〜前に』(過去形とともに使う)。
next:wr:964.relatedInfo: before(過去完了形とともに使うこともある)との対比。

next:wr:966.hint: 彼が何を言っているのかほとんど聞き取れなかった(程度)
next:wr:966.answer: I could hardly hear what he was saying.
next:wr:966.fullSentence: I could hardly hear what he was saying.
next:wr:966.explanation: hardly = scarcely『ほとんど〜ない(程度)』。

next:wr:968.hint: 彼女はファストフードをほとんど食べない
next:wr:968.answer: She hardly ever eats fast food.
next:wr:968.fullSentence: She hardly ever eats fast food.

next:wr:970.hint: そのプロジェクトはほとんど終わっている
next:wr:970.relatedInfo: ほぼ同じ意味で使い分けは大きくない。

next:wr:972.hint: 私たちが着いたとき、電車はまさに出発するところだった
next:wr:972.answer: The train was about to leave when we arrived.
next:wr:972.fullSentence: The train was about to leave when we arrived.
next:wr:972.explanation: be about to do『まさに〜するところだ』。
next:wr:972.relatedInfo: 直前の未来を表す表現。

next:wr:974.hint: 彼女は荷物を2つ運んでいた
next:wr:974.answer: She was carrying two pieces of baggage.
next:wr:974.fullSentence: She was carrying two pieces of baggage.
next:wr:974.explanation: two pieces of baggage『荷物2つ』。baggageは不可算名詞なのでpiece(s) ofで数える。

next:wr:976.hint: この件には疑いの余地がない
next:wr:976.answer: There is no room for doubt in this case.
next:wr:976.fullSentence: There is no room for doubt in this case.
next:wr:976.explanation: There is no room for A.『Aの余地がない』。
next:wr:976.relatedInfo: There is room for A.の否定形。

next:wr:978.hint: このソファはたくさんスペースをとる
next:wr:978.answer: This sofa takes up a lot of room.
next:wr:978.fullSentence: This sofa takes up a lot of room.
next:wr:978.explanation: take up a lot of room『たくさんスペースをとる』。
next:wr:978.relatedInfo: take upは『(場所・時間を)占める』の意味。

next:wr:979.hint: 繁華街までのバスの運賃はいくらですか
next:wr:979.answer: How much is the bus fare to downtown?
next:wr:979.fullSentence: How much is the bus fare to downtown?
next:wr:979.relatedInfo: feeやchargeと混同しやすい料金関連語彙のグループ。

next:wr:981.hint: 労働者たちはより高い賃金を要求した

next:wr:983.hint: その値段には消費税が含まれている
next:wr:983.relatedInfo: 料金関連語彙のグループの一つ。

next:wr:985.hint: その旅行の総費用は予想より高かった
next:wr:985.answer: The total cost of the trip was higher than expected.
next:wr:985.fullSentence: The total cost of the trip was higher than expected.
next:wr:985.relatedInfo: 料金関連語彙の中でも最も一般的な語。

next:wr:987.hint: その慈善団体は病院のために資金を集めた
next:wr:987.answer: The charity raised funds for the hospital.
next:wr:987.fullSentence: The charity raised funds for the hospital.
